methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $75M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Sofar Ocean is a Series B-stage company in the Ocean & Maritime sector founded by Tim Janssen and Evan Shapiro. The company has raised $75M+ to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of publicly traded comparables in this subsector and limited access to recent private transaction data for direct peers, reducing the robustness of traditional multiples-based approaches.

Given these data limitations, the Stage-Progression method was applied as the primary valuation framework. Using total capital raised of $75M as a proxy for post-money value at the most recent financing event, a 1.9x step-up multiplier was applied to reflect typical Series B to subsequent-stage progression dynamics. This yields an implied valuation of $142M. A sensitivity range was constructed around this central estimate: the low case of $121M assumes a 1.6x multiplier, while the high case of $164M assumes a 2.2x multiplier, bracketing uncertainty in stage-to-stage progression rates for hardware-enabled maritime technology ventures.

The analysis supports a median valuation of $142M, with a reasonable range of $121M to $164M. Key uncertainties include the absence of public market comparables for validation, limited visibility into the timing and terms of the Series B round (which would refine the base valuation), and execution risk specific to ocean-based hardware commercialization. Investors should seek additional private transaction data and customer traction metrics to narrow this range.
